title: A true joint-data risk has a positive empirical replacement budget
source_anchor: Samplinglib original quadratic feature-risk supplement v1, interface6
target_statement: Let W be measurable with measurable singleton points, X measurable, and P a probability measure on X×R with input marginal PX=P.map fst. Let K:W->X->R. Suppose each K(q) is genuinely in L²(PX), every corresponding L² norm is at most the same b>0, and the true response coordinate z↦z.2 is in L²(P). For any N>0, configuration w:Fin N->W, index i and replacement u, define rho=N^{-1} sum_j Dirac(w_j), rhoNew by replacing only index i, predictor_law(x)=integral K(q,x) dlaw(q), risk(law)=integral(predictor_law(z.1)-z.2)² dP(z), and V(q)=2 integral(predictor_rho(z.1)-z.2)K(q,z.1) dP(z). Put D=integral V drhoNew-integral V drho. Then4b²>0; both empirical laws are probabilities; both actual losses and both finite-law potential integrals are integrable; D=(V(u)-V(w_i))/N; and risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-D equals the input-marginal integral of (predictor_rhoNew-predictor_rho)². This remainder is nonnegative and at most4b²/N². No independence of input and response, global parameter measurability, or assumed pairing/remainder/displacement bound is used.
